title: The root names the chord
summary: Find the note the chord is built from.

steps.title: The root names the chord
steps.body:
**root** means the note a chord is built from and named after. The root of a C chord is C. Today our simple C, E, G example has C at the bottom too; the root is the chord’s name, not a rule that it must always be the lowest sound.

**Why it matters:** The root helps you name a chord and build it from the correct starting note.

steps.title: Read and hear the notes
steps.body: C is the root. E and G complete this C chord. Play C3 by itself, then put E and G beside it.

steps.title: Make it familiar
steps.body: Find a C on another string. Play the same C chord with that C; listen for the same family of sounds.

items.prompt: What is the root of this chord?
Play C, E, G together. Use any positions for these notes.
